records.summary: Characters who begin the game with exposure to temporal distortion may select the Timewalker background. 🧍 Timewalker (Background Perk) Once per session, ask one question, or swap a prepared ability/weapon. Chrono Snap 2,000 XP Rewind the last round of combat for yourself. You regain all movement, action, and reactions—but cannot use the same actions twice. Timeline Fork 3,000 XP After a rest, choose a “saved” version of your character. If you die or lose sanity, you may return to that state, once per campaign arc. Loopcaster 4,000 XP Trap a 30-ft area in a 12-second loop for 2 rounds. Creatures reroll saving throws and repeat actions unless they succeed on a Will or Logic save. Quantum Blink 5,000 XP You may move instantaneously to any location youʼve visited in this timeline, once per day. High risk in collapsed timelines.

- For traps that trigger over time (like collapsing ceilings or poison clouds), players must race against the clock. Each round becomes critical as they navigate or escape the trap's range. ---
- Some traps are linked in chains, where triggering one activates others in sequence. Players must stay alert and think ahead to avoid cascading damage or debuffs. ---

Effect: Releases toxic gas in a 20-ft radius, dealing 3d8 poison damage. Targets must make a Constitution Save (DC 15) or become poisoned for 1d6 rounds. Trigger: Motion sensor (DC 12 to detect). Duration: 1 round, lingering effect for 1d6 rounds.

Effect: Deals 2d12 lightning damage to all targets in a 15-ft radius and causes "shocked" condition, giving disadvantage on Dexterity checks. Trigger: Proximity sensor (DC 13 to detect). Duration: Lasts 2 rounds or until deactivated.
Effect: Pulls targets in a 20-ft radius toward the center, halving movement speed and dealing 1d8 bludgeoning damage each turn. Trigger: Tripwire or timer (DC 14 to spot). Duration: 3 rounds.

Effect: Target sinks into quicksand and takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage per round while immobilized. The quicksand explodes on trigger, dealing an additional 3d8 fire damage. Trigger: Weight threshold (DC 16 to detect). Duration: Until escaped or disabled.
Effect: Engulfs a 10-ft area in flames, dealing 3d10 fire damage. Targets in range must make a Dexterity Save (DC 15) or take full damage. Trigger: Pressure plate or timer. Duration: 1 round.

Effect: Deals 3d6 necrotic damage and causes fear for 1d4 rounds (Wisdom Save DC 16 to resist). Trigger: Proximity (DC 15 Arcana to detect). Duration: Immediate on trigger, fear effect lasts 1d4 rounds.
Effect: Drains 1d6 life force per turn and causes blindness if failed Wisdom Save (DC 16). Trigger: Arcane touch sensor (DC 15 to detect). Duration: 1d4 rounds.

Effect: Targets are pinned to the ground, taking 2d8 bludgeoning damage and having movement speed reduced to 0. Trigger: Contact plate (DC 15 to spot). Duration: 1d4 rounds or until Strength Save (DC 15) is made.

Effect: Causes memory loss and confusion in a 15-ft radius (Intelligence Save DC 16). Affected creatures forget the last 1d4 rounds. Trigger: Proximity or touch sensor. Duration: Immediate, with memory loss lasting 1d4 rounds.
Effect: Drains 2d4 hit points and prevents healing for 1d6 rounds (Wisdom Save DC 17 to resist). Trigger: Aura sensor (DC 18 Arcana to detect). Duration: 1 round with lingering effect for 1d6 rounds.

Effect: Emits a concussive sound wave, dealing 2d10 thunder damage and deafening targets in a 20-ft radius. Targets must succeed on a Constitution Save (DC 14) or be deafened. Trigger: Proximity or tripwire. Duration: 1 round.
Effect: Freezes time in a 10-ft radius, immobilizing all creatures for 1d4 turns (no save). Trigger: Proximity (DC 18 Arcana to detect). Duration: Instantaneous.

•Rog NPCs may treat Furashin with subtle condescension or formal distance, using terms like “wanderer folk” or “loosed echoes.” •Furashin PCs may instinctively distrust Rog characters—even benevolent ones—and may require narrative justification for cooperation. •Long-term campaigns may explore forgiveness, vengeance, or reparation arcs, especially if players directly face remnants of slave-era outposts or discover evidence of a shared ancestry.

records.proposedName: The Silent Sky and the Star Alone
records.summary: The sky above Apogine is a gray void pierced only by one dim sun and one ghostly moon. No stars. No constellations. No galaxies. It is the final sky of a dead reality. •Game Effect: Any navigation by celestial orientation is impossible. Madness checks (DC 13) may be required for characters unaccustomed to the void above.
•Void Nexuses are invisible entropy wells found deep within ruins or beneath collapsed layers. •Any character who spends 1 hour near one must make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw:

•A successful Wisdom (Survival) or Intelligence (Navigation) check (DC 15) is required daily to stay on course. Failure results in the ship drifting off course, adding 1d6 hours or days to the journey. 2.Managing the Ship: •Ships require coordinated effort to sail. Players assigned to the helm, sails, lookout, and rigging must work together to maintain speed and direction. •Poor teamwork or failed navigation rolls may cause sails to rip or rigging to come loose, reducing movement speed until repaired. 3.Crossing Dangerous Waters: •Certain areas, such as reefs, pirate territories, or waters patrolled by sea monsters, demand Dexterity (Vehicle Handling) checks (DC 14). A failed check results in damage to the ship or an encounter.
•Strong currents pull swimmers deeper into trenches or caves. Players must succeed on Strength (Athletics) checks (DC 14) to escape, or they risk being dragged into unknown regions.

•Herons and Kingfishers: Birds that lead travelers toward water routes or fish. Observing these creatures can provide players with hints about safe water crossings. •Swamp Spirits (Optional): Ancient nature spirits that protect the mangrove swamp. Players who treat the swamp with respect may gain their favor, while those who disrespect it may invoke their wrath. 3.Useful Plants: •Mangrove Bark: When boiled, it creates a bitter tea that helps recover from disease and infection, granting advantage on Constitution saving throws against disease. •Siltroot: A rare plant found only in the deepest parts of the swamp. Its juice acts as a healing salve, restoring 1d8 HP when applied. •Spore Caps: Large mushrooms that release a cloud of spores when disturbed. The spores cause drowsiness (Constitution saving throw DC 12 or fall asleep for 1d4 minutes).

An ancient entity protects the swamp. Characters seeking its favor must perform a ritual involving rare swamp flowers and an offering of blood (1 HP from each character). 3.Lost Ruins: Deep within the swamp, characters may stumble upon overgrown ruins. Exploring them offers treasure but risks disturbing undead guardians. 4.Foul Bargain: A hag resides in the swamp, offering enchanted items in exchange for favors or souls. Her gifts are often double-edged.

•Narrow sections require Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 14) to avoid becoming stuck. Heavy armor imposes disadvantage on these checks, and getting stuck may leave characters vulnerable to predators. 3.Swimming Challenges: •In areas with strong currents or vertical drops, Strength (Athletics) checks (DC 13) determine whether players can stay on course. Failure results in 1d6 bludgeoning damage from hitting rocks.
•Some creatures, like octopuses or fish with camouflage, wait silently in the shadows. Characters must succeed on Wisdom (Perception) checks (DC 14) to spot these threats before itʼs too late.

•Characters swimming through certain areas may encounter creatures that deliver electric shocks. A failed Dexterity saving throw (DC 13) results in 2d8 lightning damage and disadvantage on all movement-related rolls for 1 minute. 4.Magical Wards: •Runes etched into the walls may detect intruders, releasing energy blasts or calling guardians. Wisdom (Arcana) checks (DC 14) allow players to spot and disarm these wards.
•Long voyages strain supplies. Players must make Wisdom (Survival) checks (DC 13) to ration food and water properly. Failure leads to dehydration and starvation, imposing exhaustion.

•Dense jungles contain plants and insects that cause infections or parasitic infestations. Characters with untreated injuries must make Constitution saves (DC 13) or suffer additional HP loss over time. 4.Tidal Currents: •Powerful underwater currents can drag swimmers out to sea. Characters caught in these currents must succeed on Strength (Athletics) checks (DC 14) to escape.
•Certain corals or sea creatures release venom on contact. Players touching them must succeed on Constitution saving throws (DC 13) or take 2d8 poison damage and become paralyzed for 1d4 rounds.
•Characters moving through coral reefs or kelp forests must succeed on Dexterity saving throws (DC 13) or become restrained until freed by another character or a successful Strength check (DC 12).

•Touching certain plants releases toxic spores into the water. Players exposed must succeed on Constitution saving throws (DC 13) or suffer 2d8 poison damage and disadvantage on future saving throws for 1 hour.

•Crocodiles lurk beneath the waterʼs surface, waiting for prey. Characters walking near the water's edge or traveling by boat must succeed on a Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 15) to spot them before they attack. A failed check results in an ambush, and the crocodile may grapple a target.

1.Smugglers or Pirates: •The isolated nature of the mangrove swamp makes it a perfect hideout for smugglers, pirates, or criminal groups. Players might encounter these groups trading illegal goods, engaging in black- market deals, or hiding from law enforcement. They may try to hire, bribe, or fight the party. 2.Ancient Ruins: •The swamp may contain the ruins of an ancient civilization, buried beneath the mud and trees. Exploring these areas offers treasure but can also awaken guardians, spirits, or traps long forgotten. 3.Mysterious Beacons: •Strange lights flicker deep within the swamp. These might lead to treasure or trap players by luring them into dangerous areas inhabited by dangerous creatures. 4.Flooding Channels: •Sudden storms may cause water levels to rise rapidly, flooding areas of the swamp. Players must quickly find higher ground or be swept into deeper water.

1.Terrain Types: •Tangled Roots: The exposed roots of mangrove trees create difficult terrain. Characters moving through this area have their speed reduced by half, and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 14) are required to avoid tripping or becoming entangled. •Mud Flats: Thick, sinking mud can trap characters. If moving through a mud flat, characters must make a Strength (Athletics) check (DC 12) every 15 minutes to avoid becoming stuck. Failure results in being restrained until freed. •Shallow Water Channels: These narrow, winding channels run through the swamp, requiring a boat for easy travel.
